question: Which instruction spellings does MSC 6.00AX (/AL /Os /Gs /Oi) use for zero tests, zeroing, argument cleanup, frame teardown after a call, far-pointer copies, byte stores from int parameters and absolute far reads, and does an _asm body always get a BP frame with 'mov sp,bp'? Used to classify ASM claims (worker asmrole, build/workers/asmrole/classify.py). Positive controls: every accepted C module (e.g. 'pop bx' cleanup and 'or ax,ax' tests throughout root:0AD9); the probe reproduces the MSC spellings. Negative contrast: ASM claims that spell the same operations 'and ax,ax', 'mov ax,0', 'pop ax' after a call, 'add sp,N; pop bp', 'les bx,[x]; mov [y],bx; mov [y+2],es', 'mov ax,[bp+6]; mov [x],al', 'mov es,ax; mov ax,es:[46Ch]' (f_1B05_018E, f_1B05_022A, f_1B4E_003B, o02_3126_005C, o00_31AD_1659, f_1F58_0006) and procs using int/xlat/lods without a BP frame (f_195A_0018, o00_31AD_1468). Caveat: the string intrinsics do emit 'xor ax,ax', 'xchg si,di' and 'mov ax,ds; mov es,ax' (variants strlen/memcpy_ox), so those spellings alone exclude nothing.
header:
#include <string.h>
extern int near g; extern int near h; extern char near cb; extern char far * near fp1; extern char far * near fp2; extern char near a[40]; extern int near n; extern int far close(int); extern int far open(char far *, int);

variants.ret0: int far f(char far *p) { h = open(p, 0x8000); if (h <= 0) return 0; return 1; }
variants.bytestore: void far f(int x) { cb = x; }
variants.gs_noloc: void far f(int x) { g = x; }

expect.ret0@0: lcall 0, 0; mov sp, bp; mov word ptr [0], ax; or ax, ax; jg 0x1f; sub ax, ax; pop bp; retf
expect.call1_void@0: push word ptr [0]; lcall 0, 0; pop bx; retf
expect.fpcopy@0: mov ax, word ptr [0]; mov dx, word ptr [2]; mov word ptr [0], ax; mov word ptr [2], dx; retf
expect.bytestore@0: mov al, byte ptr [bp + 6]; mov byte ptr [0], al
expect.bios@0: sub bx, bx; mov es, bx; mov bx, 0x46c; mov ax, word ptr es:[bx]
expect.asm_noframe@0: push bp; mov bp, sp; int 0x10; mov sp, bp; pop bp; retf
